absent: Exact numeric values of state bits, flags and error codes beyond their roles in filtering, idle setup and validation.
Callers and triggering conditions for dump, migration, attach and cpuset helpers beyond their local contracts.
Full runqueue, entity and task layouts beyond members observed by debug printers and idle setup.
Scheduling decisions, wakeup paths and balancing behavior beyond reporting and idle initialization.
Internal behavior of cross dossier helpers for locking, time, masks, tracing and arithmetic beyond invocation points.

findings.text: Task listing service accepts a state mask and walks every thread, emitting only matching tasks through the single task dumper, while an empty mask additionally triggers full scheduler debug and global lock reporting.
Scheduler debug service emits a global header followed by one per processor section for every online processor, refreshing supervision state around each processor to tolerate slow output.

Per task scheduler report presents identity and thread count, execution and virtual time, migration and switch totals, optional detailed statistics when enabled, plus load, utilization, policy and NUMA context.
Per processor class reports walk the fair leaf queues, the realtime queues and the deadline queue for the target processor and delegate formatting to the corresponding queue printer.

Boot time idle preparation binds a task to its processor as a per processor kernel thread, links it as runqueue idle and current occupant, assigns the idle scheduling class and initializes tracing, virtual time and naming.
Affinity and placement helpers expose cpuset shrink validation, attach veto for threads that forbid affinity changes, and cross processor migration with same processor shortcut and mask validation.

An empty mask matches every task; a nonempty mask requires overlap with sampled state, with an added exclusion that keeps load exempt idle tasks out of a pure uninterruptible query while still allowing killable sleepers.
Global lock information appears only on unfiltered dumps; filtered dumps restrict output to matching tasks.
Debug output abstraction directs formatted text either to a sequence file when present or to the kernel log continuation path otherwise, preserving a single call site for both sinks.
Nanosecond quantities are rendered as paired high and low components rather than a single integer, used consistently for clocks, runtimes, deadlines and statistics.
Detailed scheduler statistics appear only when the statistics gate reports enabled; otherwise related sums are shown as zero or omitted while core identity and load fields remain.
Runqueue table printer restricts rows to tasks whose current processor equals the requested processor and marks the running occupant distinctly from other states.
NUMA reporting tolerates absence: group identifier falls back to zero without a group, and fault breakdown prints zeros when per task or group counters are unavailable.

Formatting helpers provide width aligned decimal and split time renderings for queue, entity and task fields, with statistic variants that read through the statistics accessor and masked variants for estimation fields.
Rightmost fair entity selection returns absent when the timeline tree is empty and otherwise resolves the final node to its enclosing entity.
Realtime queue iteration has two shapes: grouped configuration walks per processor queues across task groups, while nongrouped configuration visits the single runqueue realtime object exactly once.

Thread walks and NUMA group dereferences occur under read side critical sections covering the whole iteration, including filtered dumps, runnable tables, fair and realtime queue walks and fault accounting.
Fair queue debug snapshots tree endpoints and aggregate accumulators while holding the runqueue lock with interrupts saved, then releases before any formatting.
Idle creation nests the task priority lock outside the runqueue lock, performs processor assignment under read side protection, and defers preempt count setup until after both locks are released.
Clock sampling for the debug header and virtual time initialization for idle tasks run with local interrupts masked, the latter also guarded by a sequence count write section.
Group path rendering prefers acquiring the debug spin protection; on contention it formats into a small stack buffer with truncation marking instead of blocking.
Deadline cpuset validation holds scheduler read side protection while selecting the bandwidth object and additionally serializes the overflow check with the bandwidth lock and interrupts masked.
Observed runqueue state includes runnable and switch totals, uninterruptible count, balance and clock values, current occupant reference, idle balance costs, plus class subqueues and bandwidth roots.

Observed task scheduler state includes sampled execution state, identity and command name, priority and policy, fair entity timing and load, switch counters, optional statistics block, utilization estimates, clamping requests, node and migration data.

Fair entity and queue aggregates expose start, virtual, deadline and accumulated times, weight and hierarchical load, averaged load and utilization with sums, plus queue level tree extremes, spread, weighting and throttling where configured.
Filter outcome progresses from empty acceptance through overlap evaluation to idle exclusion refinement and final acceptance, yielding one boolean per task.

Migration progresses from same processor success through affinity rejection to traced stopper based transfer, while cpuset shrink validation progresses from empty acceptance through bandwidth overflow evaluation to a boolean result.
Per task averages derive from accumulated runtime divided by switch or migration totals, with a negative sentinel substituted when the divisor is zero to signal undefined rather than zero.
Boot entry establishes the per processor idle thread; operational entries expose filtered task dumps, global scheduler debug, per task sequence output and NUMA fault breakdown.
Full dumps on slow consoles can stall supervision, so the services explicitly refresh NMI and softlockup monitoring during iteration.
Formatting group paths without the debug lock risks concurrent modification, mitigated by a bounded fallback buffer with explicit truncation marking.
Sampling live runqueue trees and clocks without protection would tear; the code snapshots under the runqueue lock or with interrupts masked and formats only after release.
Scheduler debug header identifies its text protocol with a version marker at major zero minor eleven alongside release and timing fields.
Idle bring up relies on stable running, queued, kernel thread and no affinity markers plus an idle virtual time state and per processor naming convention.
Fair utilization estimation uses an unchanged sentinel mask to preserve valid bits, and task clamping distinguishes minimum and maximum request slots with effective values derived separately.
Symmetric multiprocessing initialization flag is annotated for read mostly sharing, indicating rare writes and frequent reads after setup.
